description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — August 10, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: mastra-ai/mastra is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: mastra-ai/mastra leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 26 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 26 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: mastra-ai/mastra — 14 commits today and 1 same-day mapped article, 26.4 below its current daily pace, with 9 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
openclaw/openclaw — 69 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
different-ai/openwork — No same-day commit after 97 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Watch whether Mastra gives every concurrent approval a durable destination
dailyInsight.insight: Mastra’s open core pull request #20347 supports a focused watch for teams that use approval-gated agent workflows: follow whether its per-tool-call suspension identity and serialized resume path merge and receive a public distribution note. The public proposal addresses a real control boundary—two sibling workflow calls can otherwise overwrite each other’s suspension state or race the same parent snapshot—but it remains a proposal under review, not an established guarantee.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The proposed code carries a suspended inner workflow run ID with each tool call, keys suspension data by tool-call ID, and queues resumes for a shared parent run. Its regression test exercises two suspended workflow tools when approvals arrive forward, reverse, and at once, expecting both calls to complete without stream errors.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A human approval is only meaningful when the system can associate it with the operation that asked for it. If workflow tools share a suspension record, an interface may make careful approval look reliable while a fast second click routes to the wrong run or resumes stale state.

actions.audience: Builder or operator evaluating approval-gated Mastra workflows
actions.label: Check the release boundary before relying on concurrent approvals
actions.instruction: Keep the current workflow behavior unchanged for now. Watch PR #20347 for an approving review, merge, and a release note; before enabling two concurrent approval-gated workflow tools in a shared parent run, run a disposable integration test that approves them in forward, reverse, and concurrent order and confirms each approval maps to one durable tool-call record.
actions.effort: 5 minutes now; 20–30 minutes for a disposable integration test after release

receipts.title: Route concurrent workflow approvals
receipts.supports: Shows the public failure description, proposed per-tool-call routing, persisted inner workflow run IDs, serialized resume design, focused validation claim, and that the PR remains open.

receipts.title: Route concurrent workflow approvals
receipts.supports: Shows the suspendedToolRunId handoff and the new regression test covering forward, reverse, and concurrent approval order.

confidence.basis: An inspected public PR and its linked commit agree on the narrow failure mechanism and exercise three approval orders, but the change is still open for review and has no public release receipt.

dailyInsight.limitation: The receipts show a proposed source change and focused tests. They do not prove merge, release availability, behavior in every persistence or provider configuration, or a complete authorization and race-safety review.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Withdraw or revise this watch if the PR is closed without the per-tool-call identity and serialized resume design, a public regression shows approvals still cross routes, or a released implementation uses a materially different mechanism with different limits.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for an approving review, merge and release notes, plus public coverage of the related duplicate-execution and parallel-delegation approval reports; those will show whether the identity boundary holds beyond the focused two-workflow test.
